known.summary: The TypeScript and Python reference configs turn the raw-number lint rule off for every test file (an oxlint override for eslint/no-magic-numbers, Ruff per-file-ignores for PLR2004), so a production limit copied inline into a test input passes lint and drifts, against the plan's rule that tests reuse production constants and keep literals only for expected values.

The Find scattered values number scan matches only '[0-9][0-9_.]+', so a hexadecimal, binary, or octal literal such as 0xFF is never counted as a whole value and repeated bit masks go unreported, although the plan makes this scan the repeated-literal check for Rust and Bash.
